facts.title: Plants in Moon soil
facts.text: Scientists planted tiny plants in real Moon soil brought home by Apollo astronauts. The plants grew, but slowly, and many looked stressed. Space farmers will need to help their soil!

facts.title: Lettuce from space
facts.text: Astronauts grew red romaine lettuce on the International Space Station. Scientists tested it back on Earth: it was safe to eat. Fresh salad in space is real!

facts.title: Seeds vs. cosmic rays
facts.text: About 580,000 seeds flew on a balloon high above Antarctica, where space radiation is strong. Fewer of them sprouted, and some had changed genes. That is why shields matter!

facts.title: Mice in orbit
facts.text: Mice that lived 33 days on the space station lost muscle and bone, because floating takes less strength. Scientists are testing ways to keep astronauts strong.

facts.title: Mars gravity
facts.text: On Mars you weigh only about 40% of your Earth weight. To learn what that does to muscles, scientists used soft harnesses so rats carried just 40% of their weight for 14 days.
